extracted.intended_audience: authors and reviewers submitting research articles to Nature Materials
extracted.subtask_description: Policy describing Nature Materials' option for transparent peer review: what peer-review material authors may choose to publish with their article, confidentiality limits, scope (applicability date and article type), and rationale/benefits for doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' opt-in choice to publish peer-review files
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the authors’ choice whether to make the peer-review file available online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to research articles submitted from 21 July 2025; if authors opt in, the reviewers’ comments and author rebuttals from each round of review will be collated in a file and published alongside the article. The policy offers authors the option rather than mandating publication (contrast: Nature Communications made it mandatory in 2022, Nature announced publishing all peer-review history in 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the published peer-review file
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors opt in, the reviewers’ comments and author rebuttals from each round of review will be collated in a file and published alongside the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published file is intended to reflect the dialogue between authors and reviewers; it does not include confidential comments to editors or private communications (see confidentiality rules). The journal will collate material from each round (not only final reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may remain anonymous; the journal respects their decision to remain anonymous unless they choose to be named in the peer-review statement included in articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a reviewer decides to be named in the peer-review statement, their identity is not associated with their comments in the transparent peer review file unless they sign their report. In other words, naming in the statement ≠ linking identity to individual reports unless the reviewer signs the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential communications excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments from reviewers to the editors and private communication between authors and editors, including decision letters, will remain confidential and will not be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aim is to publish the dialogue between authors and reviewers, not editorial deliberations or private correspondence; decision letters and reviewer-to-editor comments are explicitly withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of confidential or sensitive information
rubrics_metrics.description: All confidential information (for example, unpublished data and information about patients) will be omitted from the published peer-review files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal will redact or omit content that could disclose unpublished findings or sensitive patient information. The policy emphasizes protecting confidentiality and sensitive material while publishing review dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability by article type and submission date
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy applies to research articles submitted from 21 July 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets a clear temporal and article-type scope: only research articles submitted on or after that date are eligible for the opt-in transparent peer review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and expected benefits of transparent peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing peer-review history aids understanding of the scientific publication process, shows efforts made by authors, creates trust, helps readers learn from discussions, and provides recognition for reviewers' service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial frames transparent peer review as improving reproducibility, accessibility and sharability of scientific results; it is also intended to help future manuscript submissions and reviewer training by making review discussions visible. These are normative benefits motivating the policy rather than operational rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of editorial standards and constructive review
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Materials continues to uphold standards in editorial processes and aims to publish high-quality work improved through rigorous and constructive peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent peer review is presented as complementary to maintaining rigorous editorial oversight; publication of review files does not alter the expectation of constructive, high-quality peer review and editorial mediation.
